---
title: "Database"
subtitle: "One JSON document per course, a single-row account, and a view that makes dates queryable"
---

The store is deliberately small: **one table for the data**, with one row per
course holding the whole course as JSON. The document is the only source of
truth. Dated items are *queried out* of the JSON with `json_each` rather than
duplicated into a second table, so there is no synchronisation problem between
a document and its index.

A second table, `account`, holds exactly one row: the person the last login
signed in as, and the Moodle it signed in to. It is separate because it is the
one fact the course documents cannot carry --- they are keyed by course, and
the person is not a property of a course.

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS course_document (
    course_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    schema_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    fetched_at     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    last_seen_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    doc            TEXT    NOT NULL,
    shortname TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (json_extract(doc, '$.general.shortname')) STORED,
    fullname  TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (json_extract(doc, '$.general.name'))      STORED
);
```

| Column | Role |
|---|---|
| `course_id` | Moodle's own id, so a row is addressable without a lookup |
| `schema_version` | `DOCUMENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`; bumped when the shape changes |
| `fetched_at` | When this course's data was pulled |
| `last_seen_at` | When this course last appeared in a sync |
| `doc` | The whole course as JSON |
| `shortname`, `fullname` | Generated, stored columns --- listing courses needs no JSON parse |

`fetched_at` and `last_seen_at` differ on purpose. Within a sync, writing is an
upsert and never a delete, so a course that stops appearing keeps its old
`last_seen_at` --- which distinguishes an unenrolment from a failed fetch.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Rebuild semantics.** That distinction is currently moot, because a sync drops
the database first: `CourseStore(path, fresh=True)` calls `drop_database()`,
which removes the file *and* its `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars (deleting the database
alone would leave a WAL that SQLite replays into the new file). `fresh` defaults
to `False` so that only the sync may drop it --- every later pass opens the same
store to read and extend what the sync wrote. What pass 2 added is not lost
with it: an unchanged course gets its cached proposal from `extraction.json`
merged onto the rebuilt record again, without a model call.
:::

## The account

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS account (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK (id = 1),
    site_url   TEXT    NOT NULL,
    site_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    user_id    INTEGER,
    username   TEXT,
    first_name TEXT,
    last_name  TEXT,
    full_name  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);
```

Every column is a field of `core_webservice_get_site_info`, which the login
already fetches to validate the token; `ACCOUNT_FIELDS` maps Moodle's spelling
(`sitename`, `firstname`) onto the columns. `save_account()` is an
`INSERT OR REPLACE` on `id = 1`, and `CHECK (id = 1)` is the constraint that
says there is only ever one: a second account would own a second set of
courses, and `course_document` has no owner column. Signing in somewhere else
overwrites the identity rather than adding to it.

Stage 2 of the sync writes it, not stage 1 where the site info arrives ---
stage 2 opens the store with `fresh=True`, which would drop anything stage 1
had put there.

Values are stored as Moodle sends them. ZHAW returns `full_name` as
`"Fynn Fischer (T LE-T-BA-DS-24HS-T)"`, with the class group appended the same
way a lecturer gets their role appended; `view_model._user()` strips it with
the same `_ROLE_SUFFIX` the lecturer list uses, so the cleaning lives in one
place and the stored row stays faithful to the source.

What the dashboard does with it: `user.first_name` is the greeting
("Good evening, Fynn"), `user.name` and `user.organisation` are the field at
the bottom of the sidebar. Before the first sync the table is empty, `account()`
returns `None`, and all three are sent as `null` --- the greeting falls back to
the time of day alone and the sidebar shows the course count.

Connections run in WAL mode with `sqlite3.Row` as the row factory.

## The activities view

Deadlines live inside `doc` under four different keys with four different
shapes. `ACTIVITIES_VIEW` flattens them into something that behaves like a
table: one `json_each` arm per activity group, joined with `UNION ALL`.

```sql
SELECT c.course_id, c.shortname, c.fullname,
       'quiz' AS type,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.cmid')   AS cmid,
       COALESCE(json_extract(j.value, '$.origin'), 'moodle') AS origin,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.name')   AS name,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.url')    AS url,
       COALESCE(json_extract(j.value, '$.opens_at'),
                json_extract(j.value, '$.submission_start_at')) AS opens_at,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.due_at') AS due_at,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.is_graded')         AS is_graded,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.is_graded_already') AS is_graded_already,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.is_outstanding')    AS is_outstanding,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.grade_max')         AS grade_max,
       json_extract(j.value, '$.grade_achieved')    AS grade_achieved
FROM course_document c, json_each(c.doc, '$.quizzes') j
WHERE json_extract(j.value, '$.cmid') IS NOT NULL
   OR json_extract(j.value, '$.origin') = 'extracted'
```

Three details carry weight:

- The arms differ **only** in the group they walk and the type they report,
  because `document.py` has already normalised every type's deadline to
  `due_at`. The view does no date logic.
- The `COALESCE` on `opens_at` exists for workshops, which carry their open date
  as `submission_start_at`.
- The `WHERE` keeps real items and drops blank placeholders. A placeholder has
  neither a `cmid` nor an `origin`; an **extracted** item has an `origin` but no
  `cmid`, and counts. `origin` defaults to `'moodle'` in the projection, so every
  row says where it came from.

The arms are generated from `ACTIVITY_GROUPS` in `config.py`, so adding a module
type is a one-line change:

```python
ACTIVITY_GROUPS = {
    "quizzes": "quiz", "assignments": "assign",
    "workshops": "workshop", "lessons": "lesson",
}
```

## Queries

```python
store = CourseStore("moodle.sqlite")          # fresh=False: read, don't drop

store.courses()                                # id, shortname, fullname, fetched_at
store.load(31803)                              # one document, parsed
store.activities(course_id=31803, type="quiz") # via the view; undated last
store.activities(dated_only=True)
store.upcoming(days=14, outstanding_only=True) # due within n days, soonest first
store.save(document)                           # upsert one
store.save_many(documents)                     # upsert several under one last_seen_at
```

`activities()` orders by `due_at IS NULL, due_at, shortname` --- undated items
sort last rather than first, which is what a deadline list wants.

Because the document is the unit of storage, the obvious direct queries work
too:

```sql
-- every grading component above 25%, with its provenance
SELECT shortname,
       json_extract(g.value, '$.name')           AS component,
       json_extract(g.value, '$.weight_percent') AS weight,
       json_extract(g.value, '$.confidence')     AS confidence,
       json_extract(g.value, '$.source')         AS source
FROM course_document c, json_each(c.doc, '$.grading') g
WHERE weight > 25
ORDER BY weight DESC;

-- anything a model inferred rather than read plainly
SELECT shortname, json_extract(o.value, '$.name'), json_extract(o.value, '$.quote')
FROM course_document c, json_each(c.doc, '$.mandatory_onsite') o
WHERE json_extract(o.value, '$.confidence') = 'low';
```

## Document shape

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  D["course document"] --> G["general"]
  D --> A["quizzes[]<br/>assignments[]<br/>workshops[]<br/>lessons[]"]
  D --> GR["grading[]"]
  D --> MO["mandatory_onsite[]"]
  D --> S["sync"]

  G -.->|"step 1, except credits"| L1["API"]
  A -.->|"step 1 + extracted rows"| L2["both"]
  GR -.->|"step 2 only"| L3["model"]
  MO -.->|"step 2 only"| L3

  classDef api fill:#eaf4ea,stroke:#86b886
  classDef llm fill:#eef3fb,stroke:#7fa8d8
  class L1 api
  class L3 llm
```

| Key | Filled by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `general` | Step 1 | `credits` is the one exception --- step 2 only |
| `quizzes[]` … `lessons[]` | Step 1, appended to by step 2 | Extracted rows have `origin: "extracted"`, `cmid: null` |
| `grading[]` | Step 2 only | Starts `[]` |
| `mandatory_onsite[]` | Step 2 only | Starts `[]` |
| `sync` | Both | `fetched_at`, `extracted_at`, `extraction_model` |

### Reading the example

Almost everything interesting about the design is visible in it:

- **The API returned one assignment; the document has three.** The other two
  exist only in a semester-plan **PNG**, read by pass 2 and appended with
  `origin: "extracted"`, `cmid: null`, and a quote (`"Challenge 16. October **
  7P"`) that can be checked against the image.
- **`grade_achieved: null` on a submitted, gradeable assignment.** `grade_max`
  is 100 and `is_graded` is true, but the mark needs the gradebook. This is the
  single biggest gap for a frontend.
- **`is_late: true` with `is_outstanding: false`.** Submitted 1 143 seconds past
  the deadline. Both facts are kept; neither is collapsed into a status string.
- **`credits: null` even after pass 2.** No document in this course states its
  ECTS, and the model proposed nothing rather than guessing --- which is the
  correct answer. Of five courses, one got credits filled.
- **`confidence` varies within one course.** The 80/20 split is `high` and
  quotable from the logistics PDF; the challenge dates are `medium` because they
  come from a screenshot; one pitch date not stated as mandatory came back `low`.
  A UI should treat anything below `high` as needing a glance.
- **`"nal"` in two quotes.** A PDF text-extraction artefact (the *fi* ligature in
  "final"). Quotes are stored exactly as extracted, including flaws --- a cleaned
  quote could no longer be found in the source.

## Alternate output

`main_test.py` also writes `course_documents.txt`: the same documents
pretty-printed with `ensure_ascii=False`, one block per course. It exists for
reading and diffing by eye --- German umlauts stay readable instead of becoming
`Ö`.
